claims.text: Conventional automotive exhaust catalysts use Pt nanoparticles on CeO2–ZrO2 mixed-oxide supports.
Controlled ALD can produce initially atomically dispersed Pt sites on CeO2–ZrO2.
Oxygen vacancies and additional anchoring agents can stabilize atomically dispersed Pt on CeO2–ZrO2.
Single-atom Pt dispersion enhances strong metal–support interaction on CeO2–ZrO2.
Atomically dispersing Pt maximizes Pt utilization.
The proposed Pt single-atom configuration promotes efficient oxygen storage and release.
Efficient oxygen storage and release improves exhaust oxidation reactions.
Additional stabilization strategies mitigate Pt agglomeration during prolonged thermal stress.
Mitigating agglomeration preserves Pt dispersion and sustained catalytic performance.
The optimized single-atom catalyst can reduce Pt loading or consumption by about 50% relative to the conventional nanoparticle catalyst.
At roughly half the conventional Pt loading, the optimized catalyst will provide comparable or greater CO conversion under simulated exhaust conditions.
At roughly half the conventional Pt loading, the optimized catalyst will provide comparable or greater hydrocarbon conversion under simulated exhaust conditions.
At roughly half the conventional Pt loading, the optimized catalyst will provide comparable or greater NOx conversion under simulated exhaust conditions.
The optimized single-atom catalyst will have superior durability during extended high-temperature cycling.
The predicted benefits will hold during cycling up to approximately 800°C in alternating oxidizing and reducing atmospheres.
